<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel app/packages: Fortify v1, Framework v12, Prompts v0, Socialite v5, Flux Free v2, Livewire v4, Boost v2, MCP v0, Pail v1, Pint v1, Sail v1, Pest v4, PHPUnit v12.

Activate relevant skills whenever working in their domains: `fluxui-development` (Flux/UI/forms), `livewire-development` (Livewire/reactivity), `pest-testing` (tests), `tailwindcss-development` (Tailwind/styling), `developing-with-fortify` (authentication).

Follow existing conventions; inspect sibling files when editing. Use descriptive names and reuse existing components. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change dependencies without approval. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested. Be concise.

Use Laravel Boost tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` to verify Artisan parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs. Use `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging, `database-query` for read-only database access, `database-schema` before migrations/models, and `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only. Always use `search-docs` for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem, Pest, Tailwind, and Fortify documentation before code changes; use broad, simple topic queries, multiple queries where useful; do not include package names in queries. Query syntax: word stemming; space means AND; quotes exact phrases; mixed terms combine AND; multiple queries are OR.

If frontend changes are not visible, ask the user to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. If Vite manifest errors occur, run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Always use curly braces for control structures. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion (`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`). Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private. Always declare explicit return types and parameter type hints. Prefer TitleCase Enum keys. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments; never use comments within code unless logic is exceptionally complex. Add array-shape PHPDoc when appropriate.

Every change must be programmatically tested: write/update tests and run affected tests. Run the minimum tests using `php artisan test --compact` with a filename/filter. Run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues. Do NOT delete tests without approval.

=== Laravel ===
Use `php artisan make:` commands for new files; pass `--no-interaction` and correct `--options`. Use `php artisan make:class` for generic classes. Use typed Eloquent relationships; prefer models/relationships and `Model::query()` over raw queries, `DB::`, or manual joins. Prevent N+1 with eager loading; use query builder only for very complex operations. New models should include useful factories/seeders; ask whether more are needed, using `list-artisan-commands` to check `php artisan make:model` options. Use API Resources/versioning unless existing routes do not. Always create Form Requests with rules and custom messages; inspect sibling request style. Use built-in authentication/authorization. Prefer named routes and `route()`. Queue long operations with `ShouldQueue`. Use environment variables only in config; never use `env()` outside config; use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Tests must use factories and existing states; follow existing Faker style. Create tests with `php artisan make:test --pest {name}` (feature default; `--unit` for unit tests). When modifying columns, retain all previous attributes. Limit eager loads with `$query->latest()->limit(10);`; follow project convention for `casts()` versus `$casts`.

Laravel 12 structure: middleware are configured in `bootstrap/app.php` via `Application::configure()->withMiddleware()`; `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware, exceptions, and routing; `bootstrap/providers.php` holds providers; `app\Console\Kernel.php` no longer exists; use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php`. Commands in `app/Console/Commands/` auto-register.

=== Flux ===
Flux Free includes free components/variants, not Pro. Use `<flux:*>` when available.

=== Livewire ===
Use Livewire (Alpine.js only when client-side interaction is required); state is server-side; validate and authorize actions.

=== Pest ===
Run `php artisan test --compact` or `php artisan test --compact --filter=testName`. CRITICAL: ALWAYS use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Pest documentation and updated code examples.

=== Tailwind ===
Use existing conventions. IMPORTANT: Always use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Tailwind CSS documentation and updated code examples. Never rely on training data.

=== Fortify ===
Fortify is headless authentication providing routes/controllers. IMPORTANT: Always use the `search-docs` tool for detailed Laravel Fortify patterns and documentation.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>
